Because of the internal connector problem (INT-101): searches returned nothing due to 401 errors (service token expired after a secret change), then intermittent errors put Oct 15 at risk. After the fix (secret rotation + token-renewal logic), 120/120 searches succeeded and Marc Gervais validated and closed INT-101 on Sept 17. The date stays Oct 22; the 29 Sept risk register still lists R-01 as open, which is stale.

The 22 October 2026 go-live was proposed by Boréal (Julien Moreau) on 8 September and approved by the steering committee on 10 September (Élodie Caron stated the decision, no objection raised); it is conditional on three go-live validations (security, accessibility, operations).

The 22 October date leaves about nine days before the contract period ends on 31 October; no penalty was identified for the move, but any further slip approaches contract end and an extension is not documented.
What production go-live date is currently approved, and with what reservation?

The currently approved production date is 22 October 2026. It was proposed by the vendor Boréal (Julien Moreau) on 8 September 2026, then approved at the steering committee of 10 September 2026, where Élodie Caron stated the decision after no one objected (Sophie, Marc, Olivier and Nicolas voiced no objection). The date is conditional, not a guaranteed go: it depends on three open validations, namely the security validation of SEC-210, the closure of ACC-303 (accessibility) and the approval of the runbook including rollback. Nicolas Perron, project lead since 16 September, reconfirmed this on 26 September and in his email of 27 September. As of the baseline, these three conditions are still open (SEC-210 in validation, ACC-303 open, OPS-601 open), and no document shows a go-live approval.

La date de mise en production approuvée est le 22 octobre 2026 (décision du comité du 10 septembre), mais elle est conditionnelle à trois validations : sécurité SEC-210, fermeture d'ACC-303 et runbook approuvé avec rollback.
The charter and meeting minutes M01 state 15 October; that is the initial target and is superseded by the 10 September committee decision.
PLAN-V2, PLAN-V3 and PLAN-JUNE still show 15 October (the plan was not updated, as TEAMS-0915 notes); they are stale and have no decision authority.

The go-live date moved from 15 October to 22 October 2026 because the internal connector problem (INT-101) cost more time than planned. On 8 September Boréal (Julien Moreau) only proposed the move, leaving the governance decision to the client. The steering committee approved it on 10 September, with Élodie Caron stating the decision and Sophie, Marc, Olivier and Nicolas not objecting. The original cause is now resolved: on 17 September Boréal deployed a fix and replayed 120 searches with 120 valid responses, and Marc Gervais validated it on the integration side and closed INT-101. The 18 September follow-up also records the connector as validated and closed. The 22 October date remains approved but conditional on other items (SEC-210, ACC-303, runbook), which are unrelated to the connector cause. The risk register dated 29 September still shows R-01 as open, but its comment refers to a 9 September status, so it is stale.

La cause initiale est résolue : INT-101 a été validé et fermé par Marc Gervais le 17 septembre (120/120 recherches).

The change is the move of the NOVA production target date from 15 October to 22 October 2026. It started as a proposal: on 8 September 2026 Julien Moreau (Boréal, the vendor) recommended 22 October and explicitly left the governance decision to the client. It was decided at the steering committee on 10 September 2026 (15:00-15:42): Élodie Caron, then project manager, stated the decision, asked whether anyone objected, and declared it approved after Sophie Lambert, Marc Gervais, Olivier Côté and Nicolas Perron expressed no objection or agreement. The committee as a body is therefore the approving authority, with Élodie Caron formally announcing it; no signed document is in the dossier, only the meeting transcript. The approval is conditional: Nicolas Perron stressed that 22 October is not an automatic go, and the 26 September committee tied it to three conditions (SEC-210 security validation, ACC-303 closure, runbook with rollback), which are still open at the baseline. Nothing in the dossier shows a contractual penalty, since it is an internal date.

Le comité de direction du 10 septembre 2026 a approuvé le passage du 15 au 22 octobre, annoncé par Élodie Caron, à la suite de la recommandation de Boréal (Julien Moreau) du 8 septembre, qui n'était qu'une proposition; la date reste conditionnelle à trois validations.
Treating Julien Moreau's 8 September email as the approval: it is a vendor recommendation and a proposal only.
Using the charter, PLAN-V2, PLAN-V3 (both still show 15 October) or the June plan as current: they are stale and not updated after the committee decision.
Reading the 22 October date as a guaranteed go: it is conditional on security, accessibility and operations validations.
Citing the 27 September email (E09) or the 26 September transcript as the approval date: they only restate or condition a decision taken on 10 September.
Believing the 15 October date still stands because of personal notes (PERSONAL-NOTES) or the first project manager's emails: these have no authority.
Assuming the 21 September status report (STATUS-0921) with its green cible 22 octobre confirms readiness: it is not an approval and was prepared before detailed ticket checks.

Nicolas Perron has been the project lead (chargé de projet) of NOVA since 16 September 2026. This is a documented handover announced by the previous lead, Élodie Caron, who had held the role since the 7 July 2026 kickoff and the charter. Élodie remained available for a few days only to support the transfer; no later document gives her a decision role. The planning documents are stale on this point.

Production data must be hosted in Canada, specifically Canada Central. Sophie Lambert (security) required this on 23 July 2026 in the architecture workshop. Marc, Sophie and Julien (Boréal) all agreed, and Élodie recorded it as a decision. ADR-007 (accepted, 23 July 2026) formalizes it and states that architecture v1 (East US) is superseded on this point. Implementation evidence: on 26 August 2026 Boréal (Julien Moreau) announced the migration to Canada Central as complete, with a connectivity and deployment test showing no blocker, and attached schema v2. The 27 August committee minutes record that the architecture team verified it, so the vendor claim is independently validated. Architecture v2 (25 August 2026) shows Data in Canada Central. A technical validation of the migration was required by ADR-007 before production tests.

Les données de production doivent être hébergées au Canada, dans Canada Central (ADR-007, décision du 23 juillet 2026). La mise en œuvre est confirmée par le schéma v2 et par le comité du 27 août, où l'équipe architecture a vérifié la migration annoncée par Boréal.
Architecture v1 (18 July) and the East US diagram in E02 are stale; ADR-007 supersedes them on location.
Boréal's email E03 alone is a vendor claim of delivery; the independent verification is in the 27 August committee minutes (M03).
The v2 schema exists both as an attachment to E03 and as a separate file; count it as one source, not two confirmations.
Sophie's 22 July email (E02) only asked the question and stated a wish; the decision came on 23 July in the workshop and ADR-007.
The charter and the 2026-07 plan do not mention the location and are not updated automatically after decisions.
The README requires an ADR-mandated technical validation before production tests; the dossier shows only the committee's statement of verification, not a separate technical report (not documented).
Is security accepted? Distinguish delivery from validation.

No, security is not accepted as of 2026-09-30. Boréal (Julien Moreau) delivered the SEC-210 fix to the validation environment on 19 September 2026 and considers the problem corrected based on its automated tests. That is a delivery and a vendor claim, not a validation. Sophie Lambert (security) said that she and her team must redo their scenario and confirm it themselves, and that the ticket must not be closed before security validation. On 26 September she scheduled the re-test and kept the status EN VALIDATION, and the same day's committee confirmed that security acceptance of SEC-210 has not yet been given.
